_doc: Per-page metadata for the Category-20 (Oral Care) standard renderer (tools/build-category-standard-pages.mjs). GENERATED by tools/build-standards-pages-manifest.mjs from data/standards/cat20-compiled — do not hand-edit. Numbers come from the compiled records, which are frozen derivations from the index repo's deterministic government-limit compiler; nothing numeric is authored here.

_meta.method_label: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default), Category 20 Oral Care: a formulated oral product takes the strictest applicable sovereign finished-cosmetic contaminant maximum in its as-sold basis, with the Germany BVL 2017 toothpaste tier read across to non-toothpaste oral-mucosal forms where it is stricter; an oral-care article takes the Canadian mouth-contact accessible-part lead ceiling and is otherwise held under component-level control. Species never replace totals, no ingredient purity specification anchors a finished-product cell, no migration value anchors a content cell, and no cell is occurrence-derived.
_meta.methodology_version: Method v2.0 — government-limit default (CLAUDE.md Part 19, Governing Principles v2.0)
_meta.basis_family: two declared bases, never mixed — (a) formulated oral products: finished product as placed on market, total content ug/kg as sold; (b) oral-care articles: total content per accessible part, ug/kg of that component's material. Neither basis is a dietary maximum level and neither is a migration/leachate value
method_prose: Two boundary decisions in this category are disclosed rather than assumed. FIRST, breath fresheners split by presentation: the row certifies cosmetic-presentation forms (sprays, strips, films, non-food oral tablets) on the cosmetic instrument family, and food-presented mints, gums and confectionery lozenges are routed out to Category 33 rather than certified against a cosmetic ceiling — the relevant food instrument (the FDA lead action level for candy likely to be frequently consumed by small children, 100 ug/kg) is five times stricter than this category's lead value, so the routing is in the protective direction.

SECOND, articles are not stretched onto cosmetic limits: a toothbrush, a floss, an irrigator tip and a tongue scraper each take a real article-scoped sovereign lead ceiling and a full-panel component-level control, and never a toothpaste value.

Total chromium is a control rather than a published screen value in every row because no sovereign publishes a chromium content limit for any product form in this category; hexavalent chromium is deliberately NOT registered as a method artifact here, because oral-care matrices routinely contain peroxide and persulfate oxidising systems in which the reduction of Cr(VI) to Cr(III) cannot be assumed.

Tin and aluminium are controls with declaration reconciliation rather than impurity ceilings, because stannous fluoride is an authorised active and hydrated alumina is a conventional abrasive, so both elements are present by design in compliant products.

pages.name: Breath fresheners (sprays/strips/lozenges)
pages.description: The Heavy Metal Tested & Certified heavy-metal-safety standard for breath fresheners (sprays/strips/lozenges) in Oral Care, evaluated on finished oral-care product as placed on market — total heavy-metal content per unit mass of product as sold (ug/kg). Not a dietary maximum level and not a migration/leachate value.. 5 of 11 panel analytes publish a numeric limit taken from the strictest applicable government maximum; the remainder are held under mandatory control or a substantiated not-material determination.
